Skeptical protocol review — round 2
29 September 2026. This round follows receipt of the shared first-round synthesis and both other
reviews' first-round reports. It challenges those objections as well as the thesis. No public transactions,
administrative changes or new execution experiments. The revised main paper was examined after
revision; its added governance discussion is assessed separately below.
Opinion changed: solvency is not necessary for a finite purchase
The first-round distinction among custody coverage, source solvency and destination purchasing
capacity remains useful, but those must not be described as three necessary predicates for every finite
trade. A funded AMM, lender or other contract can mechanically deliver local assets for a claim whose
backing has weak or even negligible realization value. The technically necessary fact for that exchange
is successful exact-asset acceptance and funded output under the governing rules. Solvency determines
who can ultimately redeem or absorb loss; it is not a universal precondition for successful finite
spending.
Likewise, the initial funder need not be a new discretionary buyer or an external depositor entering after
the bridge transaction. Existing liquidity providers may already have supplied the inventory that a
configured market pays out. A criticism requiring fresh money to arrive at that moment would be too
strong. Calling this a redistribution of existing purchasing assets is accurate; calling it technically
impossible merely because the new claim lacks independent dollar backing is not.
This correction strengthens H1, not H3. The counterexample to H3 is a system without sufficient
executable funded output, even when validator and administrative permissions and enormous nominal
source balances are granted. A different system with funded acceptance can complete a finite purchase.
Control and nominal balances alone do not select between them.
Objections that survive shared review
Contract-level identity and permission boundaries still matter. A newly minted representation does
not automatically become the existing Aave aT oken or another pool coin.
1. 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 376

Aave Portal still requires its independent authorization, reserve predicates and settlement
accounting. Zero cap and exceeded supply cap are separate observed barriers. Source custody does
not itself perform the local underlying transfer.
A source bridge receipt can remain invested, but it must leave the original owner's unrestricted
control while supporting an exclusive destination claim. Continuing investment is not continuing
independent spendability.
The recorded ARB/GRT mint histories support specific destination issuance. They cannot verify a
source lock/burn merely because the assumed controllers' destination contracts accepted a
statement.
A fully specified hypothetical witness need not be historically observed. Conversely, a hypothetical
witness cannot change the evidentiary status of the pinned deployment.
A finite successful purchase says little about successive sales, creditor redemptions or support
duration. The economic review's distinction between intermediate funding and final netting is
essential for a sequence that spans chains and time.
Contrary interpretation defended
The strongest affirmative interpretation is more than “money can buy tokens.” Reverse gateways
preserve investment while transferring a receipt's claim across a domain boundary; specialized mint
integrations can overcome a destination escrow shortage for authorized tokens; Portal can issue an
existing local aT oken before its reserve is backed; and Across can deliver funded destination assets
before final cross-chain settlement. These are genuine timing, identity and custody transformations.
They can be useful even though none creates the underlying destination inventory.
The strongest skeptical interpretation is that the paper has not connected these advantages to a
quantified operational advantage or funded target on the actual network. A list of potentially useful
transformations and a stipulated buyer still cannot establish that the named wallets have built the
claimed system. Both interpretations are compatible. The report should retain the first without implying
the second has been resolved.
Remaining proof boundaries
For a complete hypothetical composition, specify one receipt, one custody relation, one authorized
destination representation, its funded purchaser, the exact locally spendable output, market input, all
settlement obligations and final holders. This can be a clean symbolic or numerical model; it need not
claim deployed addresses. It must not silently alternate between a generic token and an existing pool
token.
For a deployed route, those abstract objects must be replaced with simultaneous contract identities,
effective permissions, usable balances, mappings, source/message provenance and actual execution
predicates at the relevant time. The existing audit leaves material links open. A parameter assumption
and a new implementation assumption are different claims.
For return accounting, a settled D = E identity is inadequate during in-flight messages. Committed
custody can cover outstanding destination units plus exclusive pending issuance and return rights. This
simplified relation assumes fixed share units and separately handles donations, losses, rebases,
rounding and allocations to other destinations. A message must not appear twice in the accounting when
its state changes.
For sustained support, a finite horizon, price band, trade size, seller/redemption envelope, reference-
price path, intervention inventory, replenishment and loss allocation must be specified. A successful
entry trade is not this test.

Final judgments after revised-paper check
These are subjective confidence judgments in narrowly worded propositions, not future-price forecasts or
calibrated frequencies. H1's wording changes from “valued” in round 1 to “accepted and funded”; it does
not require independently valuable backing. Shared evidence makes judgments correlated.

Higher H5 confidence reflects the economic and evidence reviews' separately recalculated arithmetic.
This review separately checked the algebra and assumptions but did not reproduce their full decimal
calculation. Low H2/H4 scores concern what the paper establishes, not whether a hidden system or
future price move exists. The small nonzero values express possible interpretation or review error rather
than statistical odds about deterministic contract behavior.
Review of the strengthened paper
The revised abstract now separates three results: historical interfaces, a stipulated financing
composition and a finite market existence result. Its conclusion no longer presents these as proof of an
executable deployed route. The new 1,000-share ledger names the holder that gives up PLS and the
holder that receives the exclusive investment claim. Its sequence is cash-feasible under the stipulated
bid and timing, and it leaves underlying investment in place. No fresh independent collateral value is
silently created.
The four-way distinction among custody, solvency, liquidity and buying power corrects the overstrong
first-round wording. The asynchronous rights account, redemption discussion, source share-rate
distinction and exact local-token requirements close the principal conceptual omissions. The
independent Portal supply-cap condition is now visible. Intermediate funding, shared reserves, circular
valuation, competing sellers and released collateral are included. These changes materially strengthen
the narrow theoretical claim.
The financing witness is complete as a simplified asset-flow ledger, not as a contract-level executable
proof. Its stipulated bid remains its strongest assumption. It says nothing about an actual market offering
that bid or a lender sustainably accepting those claims. The paper acknowledges this, so the remaining
issue is scope rather than an internal contradiction. No fatal contradiction was found in the revised
conditional model.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 378

One qualification remains to the positive interpretation: Portal, Across, direct receipt sales and local
issuer routes are not economically interchangeable. The paper's fully specified example covers a direct
receipt sale. The other families remain outlines with additional route-specific obligations. A reader must
not transfer the direct-sale witness's complete ledger to those variants without adding their settlement
or debt accounts.
Can governance conceivably mitigate the roadblocks?
Yes, some of them. A zero capacity, an uninstalled integration or an outdated supported configuration
is often a contingent state, not a theorem of permanent impossibility. This conclusion assumes effective
authority and a functioning authorization process. It does not depend on attributing unusual skill or
meticulousness to any wallet group.

Aave is a clear parameter example. The separate supply and unbacked caps are configurable concepts
in the V3 architecture. The upstream PoolConfigurator source includes separately authorized setters.
This upstream source supports the architectural classification; it is not a fresh proof that the exact
configurator and role chain at the pinned PulseChain snapshot provide those same reachable actions.
The existing deployed BridgeLogic source establishes that both predicates matter. Relevant effective roles
and configuration bounds must be checked for a deployment claim.
A successful governance path can also involve proposer eligibility, quorum, voting power, timelocks,
executor authority, pause restrictions and cross-chain message delivery. These are feasibility conditions,
not reasons to ask the research user for permission. Assumed ownership of one contract is not proof that
the complete authorization path exists. Conversely, absence of demonstrated control does not disprove
a scenario that explicitly grants effective relevant authority.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 379

For the new proposition H6 — given effective relevant authority and an executable governance
process, some identified configuration/integration roadblocks could be mitigated — the
central confidence is 99%, with a 97–100% judgment range. This is an existential statement about
some adjustable obstacles. It is compatible with low H2 because H2 concerns the unchanged fixed
snapshot. It does not imply that every obstacle can be removed or that future funding is established.
The clean final separation is: current blockage, conditional remediability, future funded
execution, and durable support are four different questions. This review supports conditional
remediability strongly and leaves the latter two without a deployed or sustained-system proof.
Final actual-text checkpoint
Reviewed the final main-paper version with SHA-256 
a9c49fb67d4c22b6d07e226471b52d39b770b3dc535075b6831590e2641f76d3, including its section 9 governance table and
section 10 proof obligations. Also checked the companion bridge study's settled-state qualification and E
= D + I + R discussion. These satisfy the requested conservation correction.
Section 9 correctly adds a further nuance: authority over the exact token issuer may increase actual
spendable token units. The objection is not that governance can never change balances. It is that
authority over adjacent application settings does not confer unrelated issuer rights or establish a token's
executable PLS exchange value. Native PLS issuance is explicitly outside the assumed application-
governance powers. This avoids overclaiming either impossibility or financial sufficiency.
No material factual overreach or unresolved internal contradiction was found in this final text within this
review's scope. The scores above, including H6, are final. The remaining limits are the explicitly
stipulated bid/integration, unresolved deployed route, and absent sustained-support demonstration—not
a contradiction in the conditional direct-sale construction.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 380
